Anybody tried using AI to model wood projects? Any tools to recommend? variodot 2 hours ago | next [–] I'm building ShopSpec ( https://shopspec.io/ ) for this kind of workflow. I'm a woodworker and use it for my own home and shop builds. It's a woodworking domain engine and parametric furniture builder focused on projects like bookshelves, cabinetry, and shop furniture. It works out the parts, joints, cut list, etc. There is an MCP component in beta ( https://shopspec.io/agents ) that allows an agent to explore designs while the engine still does the math. To take a design to CAD, a project can be exported as DXF or as a Ruby script that rebuilds it in SketchUp Pro. It's narrower than Shapr3D, but it might fit the projects you describe. reply xyst 14 minutes ago | parent | next [–] I want to self host this. The only tool I have relied on https://www.cutlistoptimizer.com/ I have found that the CAD based tools to be pretty much beside the point for _most_ wood working projects for hobbyists, for a few reasons: 1. First several 3-d design iterations are throwaway reworked because I am constantly measuring the design, clearances and studs. And paper works best here instead of working with clankers which takes way longer. 2. Choosing the right kind of materials: thickness and type of plywood, type of hinges, panels, finished or unfinished. Optimize for simplicity of putting components together is most important. 3. Once the design settles the actual joinery needs to be as simple and efficient e.g. butt joints work well most of the time. A good jig for pocket holes is generally the most needed. You will be surprised how well a staple gun works for creating back panels of cupboards. Its not that they are not useful, shopspec looks great(good job variodot), its just that I can get further and faster without them for most hobbyist pursuits. I invoke YAGNI most of the time because I constantly ask myself one question: "How can I make this be less time consuming?". reply meetingthrower 59 minutes ago | prev | next [–] I am a woodworker mostly but do it all on pencil and paper.
